Diversity Averaged over Repeated Rarefactions

Source: R/rarefied.r
rarefied_diversity.Rd

Rarefy a count table many times, compute alpha or beta diversity from each rarefied table, and average the results. A single rarefaction throws reads away at random, so its diversity values carry sampling noise; averaging many keeps rarefaction's control for uneven sequencing depth and removes most of that noise. This is mothur's dist.shared(subsample = T), vegan's avgdist(), and QIIME 2's q2-boots.

Usage

beta_div_rarefied(
  counts,
  metric,
  depth = NULL,
  times = 100L,
  average = "mean",
  sd = FALSE,
  margin = 1L,
  norm = "none",
  pseudocount = NULL,
  power = 1.5,
  alpha = 0.5,
  tree = NULL,
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  seed = 0L,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

alpha_div_rarefied(
  counts,
  metric,
  depth = NULL,
  times = 100L,
  average = "mean",
  sd = FALSE,
  cutoff = 10L,
  digits = 3L,
  tree = NULL,
  margin = 1L,
  q = 2,
  bias_corrected = TRUE,
  seed = 0L,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

counts

A count table (samples \(\times\) features) of whole numbers; see Input Types. A phyloseq, rbiom or TreeSummarizedExperiment object's tree is used for the phylogenetic metrics.

metric

The name of a diversity metric: for beta_div_rarefied(), one of beta_div()'s metrics, such as 'bray'; for alpha_div_rarefied(), one of alpha_div()'s, such as 'shannon'. Matched as those functions match it (case-insensitive, with prefixes and aliases). See list_metrics().

depth

The number of observations to rarefy every sample to: a single whole number of at least 1. Samples with fewer observations are dropped (with a warning), and are listed in the result's dropped attribute. NULL (the default) chooses the depth as rarefy() does (see "Choosing the depth").

times

The number of rarefactions to average, a whole number of at least 1. Default: 100, as vegan::avgdist().

average

How the rarefactions' values are combined: "mean" (the default), "median", or for beta_div_rarefied() only, "medoid". Case-insensitive, and a prefix is enough. See "Choosing how to average".

sd

Also return the standard deviation of each value over the times rarefactions, as attribute sd. Default: FALSE.

margin

The margin containing samples: 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored for phyloseq, rbiom and SummarizedExperiment objects. Default: 1.

norm

Normalize the incoming counts. Options are:

  • 'none': No transformation.

  • 'percent': Relative abundance (sample abundances sum to 1).

  • 'hellinger': Square root of relative abundance (the Hellinger transformation).

  • 'binary': Unweighted presence/absence (each count is either 0 or 1).

  • 'clr': Centered log ratio.

  • 'rclr': Robust centered log ratio.

  • 'log': Log relative abundance (log-TSS), with pseudocount added to every value first.

Default: 'none'.

pseudocount

Value added to counts to handle zeros when norm = 'clr' or 'log'. Ignored for other normalization methods. See Pseudocount section.

power

Only used when metric = 'minkowski'. Scaling factor for the magnitude of differences between communities (\(p\)). Default: 1.5

alpha

Only used when metric = 'generalized_unifrac'. How much weight to give to relative abundances; a value between 0 and 1, inclusive. Setting alpha=1 is equivalent to normalized_unifrac().

tree

Only used by phylogeny-aware metrics. A phylo-class object representing the phylogenetic tree for the OTUs in counts. The OTU identifiers given by colnames(counts) must be present in tree. Can be omitted if a tree is embedded with the counts object or as attr(counts, 'tree').

pairs

Which pairs of samples to compute distances for, as in beta_div(): indexes into the distance matrix of the samples that are kept (not dropped for having fewer than depth observations), as with beta_div(rarefy(counts, depth), metric, pairs = pairs). Default: NULL (all pairs).

clust

Whether and how to cluster the samples (rows and columns) before returning the distance matrix: NULL (the default) or FALSE to keep them in their input order, or one of stats::hclust()'s linkage methods, "average" (UPGMA), "complete", "single", "ward.D", "ward.D2", "mcquitty" (WPGMA), "median" or "centroid", or "pcoa" to order them along the first axis of pcoa(). Clustering reorders the samples of the result, with their labels (samples without names are labelled with their positions in the input): its order attribute gives each one's position in the input, so that meta[attr(d, "order"), ] lines metadata up with them. ecodive's ordinations and tests put the samples back in their input order before analysing them, so give them metadata in its usual order. Other packages see the reordered matrix: give them metadata reordered by order, or matched by name. The matrix's display list keeps clust (FALSE as "none"; see ecodive_display), which plot.ecodive_dist() follows: with NULL it clusters the samples for the heatmap ("average"), and with "none" it keeps their order. clust needs every distance, so it cannot be used with pairs. rho_p()'s similarities are clustered as \(1 - \rho_p\).

seed

An integer seed for the rarefactions: iteration \(t\) uses seed + t - 1, as rarefy(times = ) does. The same seed gives the same result, for any cpus. Default: 0.

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), is the CPU cores this R process may use, within any limits set on it. Results are the same for any cpus.

cutoff

The maximum number of observations to consider "rare". Default: 10.

digits

Precision of the returned values, in number of decimal places. E.g. the default digits=3 could return 6.392.

q

The order of a Hill number, or of Rényi's or Tsallis's entropy: a single number of at least 0, where Inf is allowed. Only used by hill(), renyi() and tsallis(). Default: 2, as scikit-bio (which calls it order).

bias_corrected

For Chao1 only: use the bias-corrected form (the default, as scikit-bio and QIIME 2), or the classic form when a sample has both singletons and doubletons (FALSE). See chao1().

Value

beta_div_rarefied(): a distance matrix of class c("ecodive_dist", "dist") over the kept samples, as beta_div() returns, with attribute method (the metric's ID). Its title (in its display attribute; see ecodive_display) names the metric and the rarefactions, such as "Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity (rarefied 100×)", so ordinations and tests of it are titled after it. Further attributes:

  • depth: the depth every sample was rarefied to.

  • dropped: the names (or, without names, the positions) of the samples dropped for having fewer than depth observations; empty if none.

  • sd (with sd = TRUE): the standard deviations, a distance matrix over the same samples, in the same order.

  • medoid (with average = "medoid"): the iteration \(t\) whose distance matrix was returned.

  • order (with clust): see beta_div().

alpha_div_rarefied(): a named numeric vector over the kept samples, as alpha_div() returns, with attributes depth, dropped, and with sd = TRUE, sd (a named numeric vector).

Details

  • beta_div_rarefied(): a distance matrix, as from beta_div().

  • alpha_div_rarefied(): one value per sample, as from alpha_div().

Iteration \(t\) (\(t = 1, \ldots,\) times) rarefies counts with rarefy(), with seed seed + t - 1, and computes the metric from it, exactly as beta_div(rarefy(counts, depth, seed = seed + t - 1), metric) would. So times = 1 gives the same result as that call.

When to use it

Rarefying controls for uneven sequencing depth: every sample is compared at the same number of reads, so that differences in depth don't pass for differences in diversity. McMurdie & Holmes (2014) called rarefying "inadmissible" because a single rarefaction discards data and adds noise; averaging many rarefactions answers the second objection. Schloss (2024) found rarefaction better than the alternatives at controlling for uneven sequencing effort in amplicon data, and Schloss (2026) found it better than robust Aitchison PCA (rpca()) and other compositional methods. To compare both views on your own data, ordinate both and test their agreement (see the examples).

Choosing the depth

Every sample with fewer than depth observations is dropped, the same samples from every iteration. A higher depth keeps more of each sample's information; a lower one keeps more samples. With depth = NULL, the depth is the smallest library size at which the observations kept (that depth times the number of samples with at least that many) make up at least 10% of all the observations in the table, as in rarefy(). Check attr(x, "dropped"), and choose depth yourself when the samples dropped matter.

Choosing how to average

  • "mean" (the default, as in vegan::avgdist() and mothur): the average of each value over the rarefactions. It needs one pass over them, and memory for a few distance matrices.

  • "median": the median of each value; less affected by an unusual rarefaction.

  • "medoid" (beta only): the distance matrix of the one rarefaction closest to all the others (smallest sum of Euclidean distances between the iterations' distances). Unlike the mean and the median, the result is the distance matrix of one real rarefied table, so it keeps whatever properties the metric has (such as being Euclidean), which a cell-by-cell average can lose.

q2-boots' defaults are average = "medoid" for beta diversity and average = "median" for alpha diversity; set them to get the same.

Memory and time. The mean rarefies times times. The median and the medoid need every rarefaction's value of each pair of samples at once, so for many samples they work through the pairs in blocks that fit in 256 MB (8 * times bytes per pair), rarefying the table times times for each block, with the same seeds and so the same draws. With times = 100, 500 samples (124,750 pairs) fit in one block, 1,000 samples need two, and 10,000 samples about 150. The medoid also needs a times \(\times\) times matrix, and rarefies once more at the end, for the medoid's matrix.

Is an ordination driven by depth?

envfit() fits library size onto any ordination, with a permutation p-value: envfit(ord, data.frame(log_depth = log(rowSums(counts)))). A large \(r^2\) means that the ordination still follows sequencing depth. cor(ord, log(rowSums(counts))) gives the correlation with each axis. See the examples.

Warnings

A warning raised by the metric (such as the Aitchison distance's choice of pseudocount) is given once, after all the rarefactions, however many of them raised it.

Same names in other packages

None, but vegan::avgdist() computes the same as beta_div_rarefied() with average = "mean" (or "median"), from R's random number generator, so their results agree only up to Monte Carlo error.

Differences from q2-boots

  • No bootstrap mode: rarefy() draws only without replacement, so there is no equivalent of q2-boots' replacement = True.

  • The default average is the mean, for alpha and beta diversity alike (q2-boots: the median for alpha, the medoid for beta).

  • The rarefactions are seeded with ecodive's own PCG generator, so the draws differ from q2-boots' (and from vegan's) for the same seed.

References

Raspet, I., Gehret, E., Herman, C., Meilander, J., Manley, A., Simard, A., Bolyen, E., & Caporaso, J. G. (2025). Facilitating bootstrapped and rarefaction-based microbiome diversity analysis with q2-boots. F1000Research, 14, 87. doi:10.12688/f1000research.156295.1

Schloss, P. D. (2024). Rarefaction is currently the best approach to control for uneven sequencing effort in amplicon sequence analyses. mSphere, 9, e00354-23. doi:10.1128/msphere.00354-23

Schloss, P. D. (2026). Rarefaction is better than robust Aitchison PCA and other compositional data analysis methods at controlling for uneven sequencing effort. mSystems, 11, e00930-26. doi:10.1128/msystems.00930-26

McMurdie, P. J., & Holmes, S. (2014). Waste not, want not: why rarefying microbiome data is inadmissible. PLoS Computational Biology, 10, e1003531. doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003531

See also

rarefy(), beta_div(), alpha_div(), rpca()

Examples

    # Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, averaged over 100 rarefactions to the
    # automatically chosen depth.
    dm <- beta_div_rarefied(ex_counts, 'bray')
    dm
#> # A dist: 4 samples (lower triangle)
#> # Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity (rarefied 100×)
#>       Saliva  Gums  Nose
#> Gums   0.426
#> Nose   0.972 0.973
#> Stool  0.991 0.991 0.992
#> # Attributes: method, depth, dropped
    attr(dm, 'depth')
#> [1] 345

    # With the spread over the rarefactions.
    dm <- beta_div_rarefied(ex_counts, 'bray', depth = 100, sd = TRUE)
    attr(dm, 'sd')
#> # A dist: 4 samples (lower triangle)
#> # SD of Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity (rarefied 100×)
#>        Saliva    Gums    Nose
#> Gums  0.0517
#> Nose  0.0163  0.0155
#> Stool 0.00795 0.00842 0.00757

    # q2-boots' defaults: the medoid for beta, the median for alpha.
    beta_div_rarefied(ex_counts, 'bray', depth = 100, average = 'medoid')
#> # A dist: 4 samples (lower triangle)
#> # Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity (rarefied 100×)
#>       Saliva Gums Nose
#> Gums    0.42
#> Nose    0.97 0.98
#> Stool   0.99 1    0.99
#> # Attributes: method, depth, dropped, medoid
    alpha_div_rarefied(ex_counts, 'shannon', depth = 100, average = 'median')
#>     Saliva       Gums       Nose      Stool 
#> 0.73365719 0.34836336 1.11804259 0.05600153 
#> attr(,"depth")
#> [1] 100
#> attr(,"dropped")
#> character(0)

    # Ordinations and tests are titled after the rarefied matrix.
    ord <- pcoa(dm, n_axes = 2)
    ord
#> # A matrix: 4 samples × 2 axes
#> # Principal Coordinates Analysis of Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity (rarefied 100×)
#> # % of variance: 53.5, 39.0
#>         PCoA1   PCoA2
#> Saliva -0.408 -0.0241
#> Gums   -0.41  -0.0244
#> Nose    0.369  0.519
#> Stool   0.449 -0.47
#> # Attributes: method, eig, prop, trace, correction, constant

    # Does the ordination still follow sequencing depth?
    kept <- attr(dm, 'Labels')
    envfit(ord, data.frame(log_depth = log(rowSums(ex_counts)[kept])))
#> # A data.frame: 1 × 7
#> # Fitted variables on Principal Coordinates Analysis of Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity (rarefied 100×)
#>           variable  level PCoA1 PCoA2    r2 p_value     z
#>           <chr>     <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl>
#> log_depth log_depth NA      0.6   0.8 0.358    0.83 -1.02
#> # Attributes: r2_perm, n_perm
